narrative_distance: close third, level 3-4; flat, watchful, tense
voice_principles: the glass and the pay drawer carry the fear; the hand near the button carries the choice
no emotion named that the body or a rule could imply
diction: the fittings of a night kiosk: the drawer, the glass, the button, the cameras, the strip light, the till
few adjectives, each earning its place
syntax: an occasional long sentence for one sustained action or held breath
rhythm: let a silence, or a hand not moving, be an action
imagery: blood on the sleeve, the drawer sliding, the strip light, the dark past the pumps, the empty road
her hand, and where it is, as the recurring index of the choice
dialogue: few words, both of them careful
the man never explains and Jo never names what she is afraid of; the theme is never spoken
no adverbial tags; distinct idiolects (Jo flat and practical; the man clipped and choosing each word)
avoid: thriller cliche (the twist, the reveal, the gun)
confirming the man as victim or villain
filter words (she felt / saw / realized / noticed / watched)
